content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained or delayed price spikes.
- Model underreacts to sharp downward moves (e.g., sudden drops below 40) — fails to anticipate or amplify the fall.
- Overestimates mean price level in the 30d window, especially when true outcomes show volatility or mean reversion.
- Forecasts show lag in responding to recent low prices — model holds onto high forecasts even after prices drop.
- When true prices spike sharply (e.g., >45), model often overshoots and then corrects too slowly.
- Model fails to capture “recovery” phases after sharp drops — underestimates rebound potential.
- Forecasts are overly smooth — fail to reflect volatility clustering or sudden regime shifts.
- Model overconfident in upward trends — fails to account for eventual mean reversion or policy-induced corrections.
- When history includes a recent spike, model tends to overcorrect or underestimate the magnitude of the next spike.
